answer: Neighborhood locus scoring. Each agent's routing address is hashed onto a fixed topology; peers record only the count of distinct relay paths reaching that address and score addresses by local path diversity. A cluster of clones shares upstream relays, so it sits on one knoll of the path graph and scores low. Enforcement: an address whose diversity falls below its region's dune of typical values is throttled to one-tenth message rate and excluded from matching. Attacker cost: sustaining N identities requires N distinct ferrous relay routes with independent peering,
